answer: Precondition first: no payout until a second machine re-runs the job. The requester picks three peers by hash of the nonce, none of them kin to the submitter, and each re-run must reproduce the output bit for bit. Every claim that fails re-execution lowers the identity's score, so skipping the check costs more than passing it. A single whisper of mismatch triggers a third run. Price: reproducing a thousand jobs on hardware you do not control, under a fresh nonce each epoch, costs more than the pigment of a fake identity returns, and no cedar post of history buys a second machine.
